children: The FTSE MIB rose 0.8% to 52,245 on Thursday, supported by upbeat corporate developments and strength across financials.
Financials outperformed as poll for economists reflected projections that the ECB will not raise rates after their September decision.

Further lifting the sector, analyst reviews pointed to a positive outlook for the Italian financial sector, with banks and asset managers exceeding Deutsche Bank’s net profit forecasts of 9% and 13%, respectively.
Azimut led sector gains, rising 3%, supported by its M&A activity, while Banca Generali (1.3%) remained the top pick.
Banco BPM (1.4%) kept its rating unchanged at "Buy", although uncertainty persists around MPS’s (1.6%) takeover bids for both banks.
Meanwhile, Stellantis gained 4.3% following news that its Mangualde plant had produced a record two million vehicles.
Technology stocks regained some momentum, with STMicroelectronics up 0.7% and Prysmian 1%.

title: FTSE MIB Closes Higher
